title: Flood Safety
description: Floods are among the most common and destructive natural disasters. Knowing how to prepare for, respond to, and recover from flooding can save lives and reduce damage.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.content: Flooding occurs when water overflows land that is normally dry. It can happen due to heavy rainfall, river overflow, dam failure, storm surges, or melting snow. Floods can develop slowly over days or flash floods can strike within minutes. Floodwaters can contain dangerous debris, chemicals, sewage, and electrical hazards. India experiences significant flooding during monsoon seasons, particularly in states near major rivers and coastal areas.

sections.heading: Before a Flood
sections.content: Know if you live in a flood-prone area and monitor weather alerts regularly. Elevate essential appliances and electrical systems above expected flood levels. Seal basement walls with waterproofing compounds. Create an emergency kit with food, water, medications, flashlight, battery-powered radio, first aid supplies, and important documents in waterproof bags. Identify safe evacuation routes and higher ground locations. Keep your vehicle fueled and ready. Subscribe to local emergency alert systems. Consider purchasing flood insurance if available in your area.

sections.heading: During a Flood
sections.content: Move immediately to higher ground if you are in a flood-prone area. Do not wait for official instructions if water is rising rapidly. Never walk or drive through floodwater. Just six inches of moving water can knock you down, and one foot of moving water can sweep your vehicle away. If your vehicle is trapped in water, abandon it and move to higher ground if safe to do so. Stay away from downed power lines and electrical equipment. Avoid contact with floodwater as it may be contaminated with sewage or chemicals. If you are indoors, move to the highest level but never into a closed attic as you may become trapped.

sections.heading: After a Flood
sections.content: Avoid floodwater until authorities declare it safe. Do not drink tap water until officials confirm it is safe. Use boiled or bottled water for drinking, cooking, and brushing teeth. Clean and disinfect everything that got wet as floodwater may contain contamination. Check your home for structural damage before re-entering. Wear protective clothing during cleanup. Document damage with photos for insurance purposes. Watch for signs of heat exhaustion during cleanup in hot weather. Be aware of snakes and other animals that may have entered your home during flooding.

sections.heading: Safety Precautions
sections.content: Never attempt to swim or play in floodwater. Avoid driving through flooded roads or bridges—turn around, don't drown. Stay away from riverbanks and streams during flooding as banks can become unstable. Do not use gas or electrical appliances that have been wet until they have been inspected by professionals. Be cautious of gas leaks and carbon monoxide poisoning from generators used indoors. Keep children and pets away from floodwater. Follow all evacuation orders from local authorities immediately. Help elderly or disabled neighbors evacuate if possible.
